svg.title: Downunder Voices Cartoon of the Day — The fee with a shy twin
svg.desc: Pen-and-ink editorial cartoon inside a fictional bank branch called Bank of Everywhere. A fictional small-business baker in a paper cap, checked shirt and floury apron stands at the small business desk holding a very long receipt that drapes all the way to the floor. On it he has pencilled a circle around a tiny second fee printed under the normal fee for a wages payment, and asks: One payment, one fee... so who's this little fella? Behind a glass screen, a cheerful fictional teller with a bob haircut, glasses and a cardigan replies: That's its twin. It's very shy. The branch has a wall clock, shelves of folders, a brochure stand reading Fees made simple, a pen on a chain, a counter bell, a potted plant, queue ropes, a window with venetian blinds and a poster reading We love small business.
svg.text: DOWNUNDER VOICES — CARTOON OF THE DAY
ONE PAYMENT. ONE FEE. AND ITS SHY LITTLE TWIN.
Source: ABC News, 12 November 2026 — ASIC alleges a major bank charged business customers fees its terms did not clearly disclose.
